transcriptionNote: All 83 records match the source register (row index 6 header, data from row 7; sourcePointer rows are 1-based) and the Phase 4 evaluation on every field: title, group, class, lever, target functions, function class, value index, value gap, components, affected cost, saving %, saving low/high (perVehicle and annual), baseline and technical specifics (in technicalDescription), cost mechanism, trade-offs, validation, investment, lead time, benchmark, practice note, maturity, conflicts, decision and reason, weighted score, P(success), risk-adjusted low/high, NRE, NRE shared and payback. The only deviation is 'Med' normalised to 'Medium' on 35 records (minor). The C1-C7 scores, NRE per unit and Net per unit were not carried into the records; they were omitted rather than altered. All 40 Develop ideas have their development-pack slide, and every figure on it (parts count, affected cost, saving a unit, band, chance, cost to do, payback, benchmark, text) matches the record.

duplicates.note: cool039 adds PCM at the SiC module to smooth junction temperature (no system downsizing); bev059 is battery pack - same lever, different part.
Library replaces an Inconel/steel retaining ring on surface-PM rotors; Z19 replaces IPM lamination bridges.
Different scope (vehicle heat recovery vs EDU-first designed output).
Library applies Si IGBT only to the secondary front-axle inverter; P1 replaces the single EDU (primary) module.
Library shrinks DC-link via higher switching frequency; P4 right-sizes to measured ripple.
P15 is a gate driver ASIC; add118 merges driver onto control board (that is P7).
Library applies induction machine to the secondary-axle variant / an auxiliary motor.
Flag nearest is bearing size; true match recorded separately (deep-6ffd7a7310c7).
48 V stator vs 800 V EDU stator.
Opposite direction (more layers).
Inverse move: library goes TO backlack bonding; S3 goes FROM backlack to interlock + cleat.
Library down-gauges the low-duty front motor of a twin-motor car.
deep: cast-in terminals replacing phase cables; m48d: 48 V BSG weld-to-busbar.
Overlapping balance-boss feature, but R9 primary lever is stamped end plates.
Li-Auto is variant commonisation via stack length; X2 is part-number sharing for volume price tiers.
Different mechanism (CAN-shared vehicle sensor vs thermistor relocated to busbar).
Partial overlap (hybrid ceramic only at high-speed end) - R10 primary lever is platform standardisation.
Inverse arrangement (library keeps grounding ring, R11 deletes it).
Induction hardening on final-drive pinion vs rotor shaft journals.
48 V inverter EOL/burn-in vs EDU.

benchmarkChecks.claim: BMW i4 / iX fifth-generation eDrive uses a current-excited synchronous machine (magnet-free)
Nissan Ariya uses a current-excited (wound-rotor) synchronous machine
benchmarkChecks.note: Externally excited 8-pole synchronous motor; Munro teardown summary at leandesign.com

benchmarkChecks.claim: Renault Zoe / Megane E-Tech use current-excited synchronous machines
benchmarkChecks.note: Renault: EESM in production since ZOE 2012; Megane E-Tech magnet-free EESM

benchmarkChecks.claim: Porsche Taycan and Audi e-tron GT have two-speed BEV transmissions in production
benchmarkChecks.note: Rear-axle two-speed (16:1 / 8.05:1); e-tron GT also two-speed rear (https://drivingelectric.com/reviews/40958/audi-e-tron-gt-vs-porsche-taycan-4s-performance-and-handling). Note: used for performance, not to downsize magnets as Z5 proposes.

benchmarkChecks.claim: Nissan Leaf and pre-2020 400 V BEVs use silicon IGBT traction inverters
benchmarkChecks.note: ORNL/DOE benchmarking: 18 IGBTs + 18 diodes in the LEAF power electronics module. Caveat: a 400 V benchmark; it does not show Si IGBT parity on the study's 800 V bus.

benchmarkChecks.claim: VW MEB shares one EDU (APP310) across ID.3, ID.4, ID.5 and Audi Q4 e-tron
benchmarkChecks.note: Confirmed with caveat: APP310 is the base/early-trim motor; higher trims use APP550 and the 2026 Q4 facelift moves its base version to APP350 (https://www.electrive.net/2026/04/27/audi-ueberarbeitet-den-q4-e-tron/).

benchmarkChecks.claim: VW ID.3 / ID.4 (APP310) has a direct stator-to-inverter connection (terminal block deleted)
benchmarkChecks.note: No public source found describing the APP310 phase connection; search returned only generic patents.
benchmarkChecks.rec: Qualify as 'integrated EDU, connection detail not public' or drop APP310 from the benchmark column.

benchmarkChecks.claim: GM Hummer EV (Ultium) has a direct stator-to-inverter connection
benchmarkChecks.note: GM confirms the inverter is integrated into the Ultium Drive unit, but no source describes the stator-lead/busbar joint or terminal-block deletion.
benchmarkChecks.rec: Reword to 'inverter integrated in drive unit (GM Ultium)'; the direct-weld claim is not publicly evidenced.

benchmarkChecks.claim: Practice note: shunt current sensing 'Widely used in integrated traction inverters'
benchmarkChecks.note: Only an industry trend from Hall to shunt sensing and supplier products (TI, Riedon); no named production traction inverter found. TI is still launching coreless Hall sensors for traction inverters.
benchmarkChecks.rec: Soften to 'emerging; supplier solutions available' and keep maturity under review (currently 'Proven').

benchmarkChecks.claim: Practice note: grain boundary diffusion 'Widely adopted across traction magnet supply'
benchmarkChecks.note: Partially supported: Nissan production motor with GBD cut Dy about 40%. No source quantifies wide adoption; trade press notes GBD is limited for thick magnets.
benchmarkChecks.rec: Cite the Nissan example rather than 'widely adopted'.

benchmarkChecks.claim: Practice note: inductive position sensors 'Widely adopted across recent traction drives'
benchmarkChecks.note: Supplier products (Renesas IPS2550, ams AS5715, Microchip LX34070) and trade press only; no named OEM production programme found.
benchmarkChecks.rec: Reword to 'supplier products in market; adoption growing'.
